column3: NKJV renders “the Skull” with the Latin-derived name “Calvary.”
Close to the Greek; NKJV includes Jesus' prayer “Father, forgive them …” without marking it, while the critical text marks it as doubtful.
NKJV includes “with them,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text lacks it.
NKJV includes “in letters of Greek, Latin, and Hebrew” and “This is,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “The King of the Jews, this one.”
NKJV has “If You are the Christ,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “Are You not the Christ?”
Close to the Greek; “judgment” is rendered “condemnation.”
NKJV has “said to Jesus, ‘Lord, remember me … into Your kingdom,’” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “Jesus, remember me when You come in Your kingdom.”
Close to the Greek; “land” is rendered “earth.”
NKJV has “the sun was darkened,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “the sun's light failed.”
